faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Quick answers about timing, data, and ads.

items.question: Is TriggerLab free?
items.answer: Yes. TriggerLab is free to download and use. It shows ads.

items.question: How precise is it?
items.answer: Times are taken on the device's monotonic clock and stored in microseconds. You choose whether to display seconds, tenths, hundredths or milliseconds; the stored value stays the same.

items.question: Does the timer keep running when the phone is locked?
items.answer: Yes. TriggerLab adds the time the device spent asleep, so a run measured across a locked screen stays correct.

items.question: Do I need an account?
items.answer: No. Measurements, history and profiles are stored only on your device.

items.question: Can I export my results?
items.answer: Yes. Results can be exported as CSV and shared with any app through the share sheet.

items.question: Which triggers are supported?
items.answer: This version uses manual start and stop and the volume keys. Camera, microphone and location triggers are not in this version.

items.question: Which languages does TriggerLab support?
items.answer: English, Hebrew, Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese, Korean and Chinese (Simplified).

items.question: Can I turn off personalised ads?
items.answer: Yes. Open Settings → Privacy choices to review or change ad consent. On iPhone you can also decline tracking in the App Tracking Transparency prompt.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: Privacy Policy for TriggerLab — event timer. No accounts; measurements stay on your device; ads by Google AdMob with consent.
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how Zuki Apps handles information when you use TriggerLab and the pages we publish for it.

section1.title: 1. Who we are
section1.content: The data controller is Zuki Apps. Contact details are at the end of this Policy.
section1.content2: This Policy applies to the TriggerLab app for iOS and Android and the legal pages we publish for it.

section2.title: 2. Information we collect
section2.content: TriggerLab has no accounts and we run no servers for it.
items: Measurements, names, notes, history, profiles and settings are stored only on your device and deleted when you delete them in the app or uninstall it. We never receive them.

Advertising: Google AdMob may process your device's advertising identifier, IP address and ad interactions to show and measure ads. On iOS, the advertising identifier is used only if you allow tracking.
Crash reports and diagnostics (Firebase Crashlytics): device model, OS version, app version and the technical details of a crash. They do not include your measurements.
Usage analytics (Firebase Analytics), only after you give consent: screens opened and coarse feature events. Events never contain your measurement names, notes or times.

section3.title: 3. How we use information
items: Show and measure ads (Google AdMob)
Find and fix crashes
Understand which features are used, if you consented
section3.content2: We do not sell your personal information.

section4.title: 4. Advertising and consent
section4.content: Where required, you are asked for consent before personalised ads are shown, using Google's consent form. On iOS, Apple's App Tracking Transparency prompt asks before the advertising identifier is used.
section4.content2: You can review or change ad consent in the app under Settings → Privacy choices, and limit ad tracking in your device settings.

section5.title: 5. Storage and security
section5.content: Your measurements never leave your device unless you export or share them yourself. Data sent by the SDKs is encrypted in transit.
section5.content2: Google retains advertising, crash and analytics data under its own policies.

section6.title: 6. Third-party services
section6.content: Google AdMob and Firebase (Crashlytics, Analytics) process data under Google's privacy policy.
section6.content2: CSV export uses your device's share sheet; we do not see what you share or with whom.

section7.title: 7. Your rights and children
section7.content: Depending on your region you may have rights to access or delete data. Delete all measurements in the app under Settings → Delete history, or uninstall the app. For data held by Google, see Google's privacy controls.
section7.content2: TriggerLab is not directed at children under 13.

section8.title: 8. Changes
section8.content: We may update this Policy from time to time. We will post the revised version with a new Last updated date.
